summary: System packages use bindep format and collections must declare [platform:rpm]; only profile-less entries are installed; dependencies can point to requirements.txt, bindep.txt and requirements.yml or be inline, and listing those files in a collection's build_ignore breaks the build.
questions: Example dependencies section with inline packages
Why does my execution environment build fail with build_ignore?
How do I specify bindep system packages?
Set python310 as the interpreter in an execution environment

answer_card.title: Inline dependencies example
answer_card.answer_md:
```
dependencies:
  python:
    - pywinrm
  system:
    - iputils [platform:rpm]
  galaxy:
    collections:
      - name: community.windows
      - name: ansible.utils
        version: 2.10.1
  ansible_core:
    package_pip: ansible-core==2.14.2
  ansible_runner:
    package_pip: ansible-runner==2.3.1
  python_interpreter:
    package_system: "python310"
    python_path: "/usr/bin/python3.10"
```

The build fails if `requirements.txt`, `bindep.txt` or `requirements.yml` are in a collection's `build_ignore`.
